title: The Kite That Would Not Fly
learning_objectives: Explain a problem and the fix that worked
Use the words heavy and light to compare
parent_prompts: Before reading: Sam made a kite from a paper bag. Do you think it will fly? Why?
After page 3: The kite falls every time. What could be wrong?
After reading: What did Sam take off? Why did that help?

pages.text: Sam made a kite from a paper bag and two sticks.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam at a table with a brown paper bag stretched over crossed sticks; glue and string nearby.
pages.audio_script: Sam made a kite from a paper bag and two sticks.

pages.text: Sam tied on a long tail of bottle caps. Clack, clack, clack.
pages.illustration_brief: A long string tail hung with many metal bottle caps dangling from the kite.
pages.audio_script: Sam tied on a long tail of bottle caps. Clack, clack, clack.

vocabulary.definition: The long strip that hangs from the bottom of a kite.
vocabulary.example: The kite's tail wiggled in the wind.

pages.text: Sam ran. The kite went up... and flopped down. Sam ran again. Flop.
pages.illustration_brief: Sam running on grass; the kite low behind, tail dragging on the ground.
pages.audio_script: Sam ran. The kite went up, and flopped down. Sam ran again. Flop.

pages.text: Mo landed on the tail. It sank to the grass. "Too heavy," said Sam.
pages.illustration_brief: Mo perched on the cap tail, which lies heavy on the grass; Sam frowning, thinking.
pages.audio_script: Mo landed on the tail. It sank to the grass. Too heavy, said Sam.

vocabulary.definition: Hard to lift; weighs a lot.
vocabulary.example: The bag of rice is heavy.

pages.text: Sam took off the caps. Sam tied on strips of light paper instead.
pages.illustration_brief: A pile of bottle caps on the grass; Sam knotting thin paper strips onto the tail.
pages.audio_script: Sam took off the caps. Sam tied on strips of light paper instead.

pages.text: Sam ran. Up went the kite, high and higher! The paper tail danced.
pages.illustration_brief: The kite high in the sky with a fluttering paper tail; Sam and Mo below looking up.
pages.audio_script: Sam ran. Up went the kite, high and higher! The paper tail danced.

quiz.prompt: What did Sam first tie on as a tail?
quiz.explanation: Page 2 says: Sam tied on a long tail of bottle caps.

quiz.prompt: Why did the kite keep flopping down?
quiz.explanation: The kite flopped (page 3). Sam saw the tail sink and said, too heavy (page 4).

quiz.prompt: Why did paper strips work better than caps?
quiz.explanation: The caps were heavy (page 4). Sam used light paper instead (page 5) and the kite went high (page 6).

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up what went wrong with Sam's kite and how Sam fixed it.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says kite only; with support: says it fell, with prompting; independent: tail of caps was too heavy, changed to light paper, then it flew
quiz.explanation: Stating problem and fix in own words shows cause-and-effect understanding.

items.text: Sam ties on a tail of bottle caps.
Sam swaps the caps for paper.

activities.prompt: Match the word to its meaning.

pairs.right: the strip hanging from a kite

off_screen_prompt: Hold a spoon in one hand and a tissue in the other. Which is heavy? Which is light? Drop them both and watch.
